utterance: Hi Mark, I understand you've had a cough and fever for a few days and are feeling pretty unwell. Can you tell me exactly when this started, and what the cough is like? Are you bringing up any phlegm?
reply: It started three days ago. The cough was dry and hacking at first. I've been burning up, on and off, and since yesterday I'm bringing up phlegm that's rusty and brownish, though it was clear at first.

utterance: Are you experiencing any shortness of breath, or any pain in your chest, especially when you take a deep breath or cough? And have you had any shaking chills, sore throat, or a runny nose?
reply: I'm only getting puffed going up the stairs, I got out of breath on the way in from the car park, but I'm alright sitting here. There's a sharp pain low down on the right side, near my back, it catches me when I take a deep breath or cough, started yesterday. The first night I was shaking under the doona, teeth chattering, even though I was boiling.

utterance:
Mark, I've listened to your chest and the X-ray confirms that you have community-acquired pneumonia in the lower part of your right lung. This is a bacterial chest infection. I've prescribed an antibiotic called Amoxicillin. You need to take 1 gram (two 500mg capsules) every 8 hours for 5 days. It's important you finish the course. Also, get plenty of rest, stay well hydrated, and you can take paracetamol or ibuprofen for the fever and pain. 

Because pneumonia can sometimes become severe, please go to the nearest emergency department or call an ambulance if you get more short of breath, if you feel confused, if the pain gets much worse, or if your fever doesn't improve after two days of antibiotics. Do you have any questions?
reply: No questions, just need to make sure I finish the antibiotic course. My head's clear, just a bit grumpy according to my wife, and the chest pain is a solid six when I cough or take a big breath, otherwise just a dull ache. I'll rest and stay hydrated.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Confusion or drowsiness
